title: The good shepherd (John 10:1–18)
hook: he knows his sheep by name and they know his voice

segments.voice: Yesterday, the healed man standing his ground: one thing I know. Your line was now I see.

In a crowded airport, a hundred voices blur into noise. Then someone far off says your name, and your head turns before you've decided anything. Travelers in the Middle East have described something like it with sheep: several flocks sheltering together overnight, all mixed up, and in the morning each shepherd simply calls, and his own sheep sort themselves out and follow him. The man born blind has just been thrown out of the synagogue. Right after, Jesus starts talking about sheep, voices and names.
screen: `YOUR NAME IN A CROWDED AIRPORT.` → `MIXED FLOCKS, ONE CALL.` → `RIGHT AFTER THE BLIND MAN.`

segments.voice: Jesus sets the scene: a sheepfold, a wall, a gate, a keeper at the gate. A thief climbs over the wall. The shepherd comes in by the door, and the Douay-Rheims says: "the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out." Name first, then leading. He doesn't drive them from behind with a stick; he walks ahead, and they follow a voice they know. Then another great I am: "I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd giveth his life for his sheep." A hired hand sees the wolf coming and runs, because the sheep aren't his. The good shepherd stays, and more than stays. John's word for good, kalos, also carries the sense of beautiful, noble, the real thing. Then a line about outsiders: other sheep I have, that are not of this fold; them also I must bring. Whatever else that means, the flock is bigger than the people standing there. And look where John sets this speech. A man has just been pushed out of his community for telling the truth, and Jesus went looking for him. The shepherd keeps the one who was thrown out. Some of the oldest Christian paintings, on the walls of the Roman catacombs, show a young shepherd with a lamb across his shoulders. And the fourth Sunday of Easter is called Good Shepherd Sunday, when the Church prays for vocations, for people called to shepherd others.
screen: `THE FOLD, THE GATE, THE THIEF.` · `HE CALLS THEM BY NAME.` · `THE HIRED HAND RUNS; HE STAYS.` · `THE SHEPHERD ON THE CATACOMB WALL.` · then, large: `THE GOOD SHEPHERD.`

segments.voice: Let the sounds around you come in, traffic, a fan, a bird, your own breath, without chasing any of them. Then, under all the noise, imagine your own first name said once, quietly, by someone who means you well, and let it land. If you pray, hold the line, he calleth his own sheep by name; if not, rest in the feeling of being known by name.
Kalos. The Greek word for good that also means noble, beautiful: what Jesus calls the shepherd who calls his own by name and lays down his life for them. Today's word.
Your line: he knows my name. Called by name first, then led. Day five hundred twelve.

howItsDone: On the fourth Sunday of Easter, Good Shepherd Sunday, Catholics hear a reading from John 10 at Mass, and the Church prays that day for vocations to the priesthood and religious life.

chat.says: Why is Jesus called the good shepherd?
options: He calls his sheep by name and stays when the wolf comes; he gives his life for them.
He kept real flocks near Nazareth for years before he started teaching.
He drives the flock from behind with a stick so none of them wander off.
chat.meaning: The good shepherd calls his own by name, walks ahead, and gives his life for the sheep, unlike the hired hand who runs.

sheepfold.meaning: a walled pen where sheep are kept

catacombs.meaning: underground burial places in Rome, with early Christian paintings

vocations.meaning: callings, here to shepherd others in the Church

notes: Mixed flocks sorting by the shepherd's call: framed as travelers' descriptions, not as a fact about all shepherding. Confirm the framing is acceptable.
Kalos as 'good, noble, beautiful': standard lexicon range. Confirm.
Good Shepherd images in the Roman catacombs (e.g. Callixtus, Priscilla) as among the earliest Christian paintings. Confirm.
Fourth Sunday of Easter as Good Shepherd Sunday and World Day of Prayer for Vocations. Confirm.
'Other sheep I have' (10:16) is quoted in paraphrase; its interpretation is left open on purpose.
